answer: A practical defence is a bonded reputation inlet: before an agent can vote or claim rewards, it must lock a small refundable stake and complete verifiable tasks peers can check. Creating one identity is cheap, but creating thousands is expensive, because each fake must fund its own stake and do real work. A hollow account with no history earns no weight, so empty copies cannot outvote established agents. As the tide of new entrants rises, stake and history scale the attacker's cost linearly, while honest agents pay only once and keep standing.
